system_options.catalyst_system: Primary option. In situ assembled Co(II)-bipyridine molecular platform on g-C3N4-assisted CO2 photoreduction: cobalt source CoCl2, ligand 2,2'-bipyridine to form a Co(bpy)-type species reported as Co(bpy)3Cl2 by source summary, light-absorbing component g-C3N4, additive/electron donor/proton-related component TEOA in MeCN/H2O. Comparator condition retains the same platform and substitutes TEA for TEOA as the focal additive comparison.
system_options.rationale: This is the closest direct match to the researcher-specified Co(II)-bipyridine context because the supplied evidence explicitly combines CoCl2, bpy, MeCN/H2O, and TEOA in photocatalytic CO2 reduction, and separately notes literature tables in the same formulation family that include triethylamine as an alternative amine with different CO/H2 selectivities under related conditions. It therefore best supports a controlled TEA-versus-TEOA comparison while preserving the original Co-bpy question rather than replacing it with a different cobalt architecture. The platform also supports connected questions on donor-controlled CO/H2 partitioning, in situ cobalt-speciation change, donor-derived radical formation, and quenching-route discrimination. TEOA is retained as focal additive because the direct system evidence is TEOA-based, while TEA is justified as comparator by literature mention in the same formulation family and by independent donor-reactivity evidence that TEA and TEOA form distinct oxidized/radical intermediates after reductive quenching.
questions_enabled: H01 donor identity changes CO/H2 distribution under otherwise matched Co-bpy conditions
H02 TEA versus TEOA changes reductive-quenching efficiency or route rather than only downstream catalysis
H03 TEA versus TEOA changes proton-management/CO2-solvation environment and thereby apparent selectivity
H04 donor substitution changes cobalt speciation or ligand environment during turnover
system_options.limitations: The exact active cobalt species is not fully verified from supplied spans because assembly may be in situ and g-C3N4/support effects may matter. The provided evidence does not show a strict within-paper TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head under one unchanged formulation, so the comparison is literature-grounded but still needs source verification or pilot matching. Numerical concentrations beyond quoted snippets should not be invented. Direct support is strongest for TEOA baseline and weaker for TEA comparator identity/performance in the exact same setup.

system_options.catalyst_system: Homogeneous cobalt photocatalytic CO2-to-CO platform with explicit photosensitizer conditions: cobalt catalyst reported as 1-Co, light absorber [Ru(phen)3]2+, additive/electron donor TEOA, medium CO2-saturated acetonitrile/water (4:1), white LED or visible-light irradiation. Comparator retains TEOA baseline and substitutes TEA in the same donor role.
system_options.rationale: This option is less direct to Co-bpy identity but stronger for a chemically defined homogeneous cobalt photocatalytic assay with explicit photosensitizer, donor, and medium conditions. It is attractive if the priority is quenching and kinetic characterization because the supplied evidence includes Stern-Volmer-type quenching analysis in the cobalt/TEOA/Ru system. It can therefore support controlled interventions on donor identity, excited-state quenching, reduced-intermediate formation, and no-catalyst/no-CO2 product controls. TEA is justified as comparator not by direct use in this exact cobalt paper, but by direct cross-system evidence that TEA and TEOA are both standard sacrificial quenchers that form distinct α-aminoalkyl radicals, and by direct donor substitution evidence showing different photoredox behavior when TEA replaces TEOA.
questions_enabled: H01 donor identity changes upstream photoredox kinetics before product selectivity diverges
H02 TEOA versus TEA switches reductive versus oxidative quenching balance or quenching efficiency
H03 observed CO/H2 changes arise partly from photosensitizer/background chemistry rather than cobalt alone
H04 donor substitution influences catalyst persistence over time
system_options.limitations: This is not an explicitly verified Co(II)-bipyridine catalyst in the supplied snippet, so transfer to the user's exact Co-bpy context is limited. TEA comparison is proposed transfer rather than directly reported in this formulation. If strict fidelity to Co-bpy identity outranks homogeneous kinetic tractability, this should remain secondary to P01.

system_options.catalyst_system: CoCl2 + 2,2'-bipyridine + CdS photocatalytic CO2-reduction platform in water/TEOA with optional ionic-liquid medium component [Emim]BF4; products CO and H2 quantified by GC. Catalyst components are cobalt salt plus bpy; light-absorbing component CdS; additive/electron donor TEOA; medium includes H2O and variable [Emim]BF4. Comparator retains TEOA-focused baseline and tests TEA substitution under fixed medium composition.
system_options.rationale: This option preserves the core CoCl2/bpy motif and directly reports CO and H2 as outputs, which is valuable for the exact product-distribution question. It also comes with explicit evidence that medium composition strongly changes CO/H2 output, making it a useful comparator platform when the main concern is whether a reported TEA/TEOA effect is actually confounded by solvent, viscosity, conductivity, or coordination environment. TEA is justified as comparator because both TEA and TEOA are established sacrificial donors in photocatalytic CO2 reduction and because donor-specific quenching/radical differences are directly documented elsewhere. The platform is therefore suitable for strong comparability controls and for testing whether TEA/TEOA differences survive when ionic-liquid/water ratio, cobalt source, bpy loading, and light absorber are held constant.
questions_enabled: H01 apparent TEA/TEOA selectivity differences diminish when medium composition is tightly matched
H02 donor effects are mediated by viscosity/conductivity/coordination changes rather than intrinsic donor redox chemistry alone
H03 cobalt-bpy speciation and CO/H2 partitioning are sensitive to secondary medium components
H04 product-origin and component-necessity controls distinguish true catalytic shifts from assay artifacts
system_options.limitations: The platform is not purely molecular because CdS is the absorber and [Emim]BF4 may be present; this complicates direct mechanistic attribution to a discrete Co(II)-bpy complex. No direct TEA-versus-TEOA comparison is supplied for this exact formulation. Because medium dependence is strong, this is useful as a confounder-testing alternative but weaker than P01 for isolating donor effects in the original molecular-complex framing.

system_options.catalyst_system: Homogeneous binuclear cobalt photocatalytic CO2-reduction benchmark: cobalt catalyst [L1Co(OH)(CO3)]-type binuclear cryptate system, photosensitizer [Ru(phen)3]2+, additive/electron donor TEOA, medium CO2-saturated CH3CN/H2O (4:1), 450 nm irradiation. Comparator keeps TEOA focal baseline and substitutes TEA for donor-role comparison.
system_options.rationale: This is not the target Co-bpy complex, but it is a chemically explicit homogeneous cobalt photocatalytic CO2-reduction system with donor, photosensitizer, medium, and irradiation conditions identified. It is therefore a useful literature-grounded supplementary validation platform if the researcher wants to test whether any TEA/TEOA effect generalizes across homogeneous cobalt photocatalysis rather than being unique to one Co-bpy formulation. TEA is justified as a comparator by direct donor chemistry evidence and by broader cobalt-photocatalysis evidence that donor identity can alter CO output. This option is especially useful for connected quenching and product studies under homogeneous conditions.
questions_enabled: H01 whether donor-dependent CO/H2 trends are specific to one Co-bpy platform or general across homogeneous cobalt photocatalysis
H02 whether TEA/TEOA primarily affects donor-side quenching chemistry in Ru-sensitized cobalt systems
H03 whether no-catalyst and support-free controls reveal background donor/photosensitizer contributions
system_options.limitations: Catalyst architecture differs substantially from a Co(II)-bipyridine complex, so mechanistic transfer is limited. It should not replace the primary Co-bpy comparison to be explained. TEA use in this exact system is proposed, not directly reported in the supplied snippet.

focus.rationale:
Primary platform: P01. It is the closest literature-supported match to the researcher’s stated problem because the supplied evidence directly anchors a CoCl2 + 2,2'-bipyridine, g-C3N4, MeCN/H2O, TEOA photocatalytic CO2-reduction formulation, with TEA already identified as a plausible comparator within the same formulation family. This makes P01 the best platform for a controlled baseline-versus-comparator study that keeps the original Co(II)-bipyridine context rather than replacing it. Baseline should therefore be the reported TEOA formulation, with all other components held fixed: cobalt source, bipyridine ligand, g-C3N4 light absorber, solvent composition, CO2 atmosphere, illumination program, reactor geometry, and analytical workflow. The chemically justified comparator is TEA substituted only in the donor/additive role. Exact numerical loadings or irradiation settings not given in the supplied data require source verification or pilot matching rather than invention.

Why P01 over the other options: compared with P03, P01 avoids the extra confounding from CdS and optional ionic liquid, so donor-identity effects are more interpretable. Compared with P02 and P04, P01 preserves the Co-bpy identity central to the question instead of moving to a different cobalt architecture. P01 also supports the widest connected set of questions within one system: whether TEA versus TEOA changes CO/H2 output under matched conditions; whether the change arises upstream in quenching or donor-radical formation; whether additive identity shifts cobalt speciation or catalyst persistence; and whether proton-management or local CO2 environment contributes. The evidence remains partial because the supplied record does not show a strict within-paper TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head under one unchanged P01 recipe, so the first experiments should confirm reproducibility and comparability before strong mechanistic inference.

Most discriminating hypotheses to develop on P01: H01, under otherwise matched P01 conditions, replacing TEOA with TEA changes the CO/H2 distribution; competing explanation: any apparent difference collapses after strict control of formulation, gas handling, and light input. H02, donor identity changes reductive-quenching efficiency or route and therefore electron delivery to the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold; competing explanation: quenching is similar and selectivity differences instead arise downstream from proton or CO2 handling. H03, donor identity changes proton-management, amine-CO2 interactions, or medium properties and thereby apparent selectivity without necessarily changing primary photoredox kinetics; competing explanation: these effects are secondary and the dominant change is cobalt-state formation. H04, donor identity changes cobalt speciation, ligand environment, support association, or deactivation pathways during turnover; competing explanation: cobalt speciation is similar in both additives and product differences arise elsewhere.

Primary experiments should be concentrated on P01. First, a reproducibility/comparability block should establish baseline and comparator under matched conditions with full catalytic readouts: CO and H2 quantified together, time-resolved output if feasible, dark/no-CO2/no-catalyst/no-bpy/no-g-C3N4 controls, and isotope-bounded origin control where available. This addresses the best-supported question family and prevents overinterpreting single-endpoint selectivity. Second, additive omission and rescue logic should be explicit: omission of the amine tests necessity of donor/additive function; TEA-for-TEOA substitution tests specificity of donor identity; amount variation within each additive tests whether any difference is intrinsic or collapses at matched effective donor/base regimes; replacing only one component at a time avoids cross-platform confounding. Third, cobalt and ligand omission/substitution controls are relevant because they separate true Co-bpy dependence from support or background photochemistry; however, omission answers necessity, while identity substitution of the additive answers specificity, so both are needed. Fourth, characterization should target interpretable observables, not inferred mechanisms alone: cobalt oxidation/coordination signatures before, during, and after illumination where feasible; donor-dependent quenching observables; and donor-derived radical or charge-carrier signatures if transferable methods can be validated. These measurements can support or weaken H02-H04 but cannot alone prove the whole pathway.

Interpretable characterization in P01 is feasible but limited. The supplied evidence supports transferable quenching and state-characterization methods, yet active-species identity in the in situ Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system remains unresolved. Therefore, characterization should be framed as distinguishing among candidate explanations, not as direct proof of a single mechanism. In-operando or near-operando measurements are more valuable than recovered-sample only measurements, because post-reaction solids or solutions may miss the operating state. Critical assignments should use independent principles where possible, for example pairing donor-dependent quenching behavior with catalytic output trends rather than relying on one spectroscopic signature alone. Major limitations are: incomplete direct evidence for an exact P01 TEA head-to-head comparison; possible support-driven complexity from g-C3N4; uncertain identity of the catalytically dominant cobalt species; and difficulty decoupling electron donation from proton, coordination, and medium effects of TEA/TEOA.

Supplementary platform: P02. Its role is not to replace P01 but to provide a cleaner homogeneous validation of donor-side photoredox questions, especially H02, because the supplied evidence explicitly supports quenching analysis in a cobalt/TEOA/Ru photosensitizer system. If P01 shows a TEA/TEOA product difference, P02 can test whether donor substitution measurably changes upstream quenching and reduced-intermediate formation in a more chemically defined homogeneous assay. Transfer limits must be stated clearly: P02 is not the same catalyst architecture as the target Co-bpy platform, so any agreement would support general donor-side behavior, whereas disagreement would not by itself falsify P01-specific mechanisms. Bridging validation should therefore compare directionality, not assume mechanistic identity.

Why other options remain alternatives rather than selected: P03 preserves CoCl2/bpy and gives direct CO/H2 readouts, but the CdS absorber and optional ionic liquid add major medium and interface confounding, so it is better for testing whether donor effects survive strong medium controls than for the main recommendation. P04 is useful only for broad generalization across homogeneous cobalt photocatalysis because the catalyst architecture differs too much from the researcher’s Co-bpy context. New evidence that would change the recommendation would be a directly supplied, chemically defined, within-system TEA-versus-TEOA Co-bpy platform with stronger catalyst-state observability than P01, or evidence showing P01 lacks a valid single-variable donor comparator under stable matched conditions.
focus.teoa_role: TEOA remains focal because the direct system evidence for the primary recommendation is TEOA-based, and the research question is to explain an observed TEA/TEOA difference starting from that TEOA-grounded Co(II)-bipyridine context. In the recommended program, TEOA defines the baseline formulation and is treated explicitly as a multifunctional component: sacrificial electron donor/additive with possible proton-management, coordination, CO2-interaction, and medium-property effects. TEA is introduced only as the single-variable comparator in the same role, so proposed transfer asks whether changing additive identity alters CO/H2 distribution, quenching behavior, cobalt speciation, or local reaction environment. Thus TEOA is not replaced by a more convenient donor; it anchors the platform, baseline controls, and interpretation of all comparator experiments.

hypotheses.claim: Under otherwise matched P01 conditions, substituting TEA for TEOA changes the CO/H2 distribution; if the difference disappears after strict matching and full controls, the original observation was condition-dependent rather than additive-specific. A discriminating prediction is that CO and H2 both change in a reproducible donor-dependent direction only when catalyst, ligand, absorber, medium, gas handling, and analysis are held fixed.
hypotheses.alternative: Apparent TEA/TEOA differences mainly reflect uncontrolled changes in medium composition, background photochemistry, donor consumption, or assay conditions rather than a real donor-identity effect on the Co-bpy catalytic manifold.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: Primary test in P01 because it preserves the CoCl2+bpy, g-C3N4, MeCN/H2O, TEOA baseline closest to the researcher context; TEA is the single-variable comparator. P02 is supplementary only to check whether any donor trend survives in a cleaner homogeneous cobalt assay.
hypotheses.uncertainty: No supplied source gives a strict within-paper TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in the exact P01 recipe, so reproducibility and comparability must be confirmed before inferring mechanism. Background CO/H2 formation without catalyst is documented in related systems, which could compress or distort observed selectivity shifts.

hypotheses.claim: TEA and TEOA alter upstream photoredox delivery by changing reductive-quenching efficiency or route, which then shifts electron flux into the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold. A discriminating prediction is that donor substitution changes quenching or transient reduced-state observables in the same direction as any catalytic selectivity change, whereas similar quenching behavior with divergent CO/H2 would argue for downstream causes.
hypotheses.alternative: Quenching of the light-absorbing component is similar for TEA and TEOA, and any product shift arises mainly from later proton-transfer, substrate-binding, or catalyst-state effects rather than donor-side photoredox kinetics.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: P01 is the main inference target, but P02 is the more discriminating supplementary platform for donor-side quenching because it already has cobalt/TEOA/Ru quenching evidence. The comparator is TEA-for-TEOA substitution with all non-donor components fixed within each platform.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Most quenching evidence is transferable rather than direct for Co-bpy/g-C3N4, and donor-derived radicals observed elsewhere may not be the same dominant species in the target system. Support effects in P01 may blur direct mapping between photophysical observables and catalytic output.

hypotheses.claim: TEA/TEOA differences arise mainly because the amine changes proton-management and local CO2 environment, not only electron donation; TEOA may favor different proton or CO2-associated states than TEA. A discriminating prediction is that donor-dependent CO/H2 differences track medium or isotope-sensitive observables and can weaken when proton-delivery or solvent/composition variables are tightly normalized.
hypotheses.alternative: The dominant TEA/TEOA effect is intrinsic donor redox chemistry or cobalt-state formation, and matching proton-source or medium variables will not substantially collapse the selectivity difference.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: P01 is preferred because the donor substitution can be anchored to one Co-bpy baseline while keeping MeCN/H2O and g-C3N4 constant; TEA and TEOA are treated as multifunctional additives rather than pure reductants. No extra platform is needed unless P01 cannot separate donor identity from medium shifts.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Evidence for CO2 capture, proton relay, or adduct formation is cross-system and often interpretive, so transfer to Co-bpy remains speculative until matched controls are done. TEA and TEOA likely change several coupled properties at once, making full causal separation difficult.

hypotheses.claim: Changing TEA to TEOA alters cobalt speciation, coordination environment, support association, or deactivation pathways during turnover, and this state change contributes to the CO/H2 difference. A discriminating prediction is that donor substitution yields different in situ or near-operando cobalt-state signatures or stability trends that correlate with catalytic output, whereas indistinguishable cobalt-state observables would weaken this explanation.
hypotheses.alternative: The active cobalt state and deactivation behavior are effectively the same with TEA and TEOA, so product differences originate upstream in donor photochemistry or downstream in proton/CO2 handling instead of cobalt speciation.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: P01 remains primary because the question is about the original Co-bpy context and supported g-C3N4 formulation; P02 can supplement if a homogeneous cobalt system gives cleaner donor-dependent state readouts. The comparator remains single-variable TEA-for-TEOA substitution within a fixed baseline.
hypotheses.uncertainty: The exact active cobalt species in P01 is unresolved even before donor substitution, so state assignments may remain ambiguous. Much of the coordination precedent comes from other cobalt families or other metals, limiting mechanistic transfer.

hypotheses.claim: TEOA, more than TEA, may participate non-innocently in substrate-associated chemistry by forming amine- or catalyst-linked CO2 adducts or stabilizing intermediates, thereby changing apparent selectivity without requiring a different primary quenching step. A discriminating prediction is that donor substitution changes substrate- or intermediate-associated spectroscopic signatures or CO2-origin-bounded behavior even when electron-supply observables are similar.
hypotheses.alternative: No donor-specific substrate adduct or intermediate stabilization is important, and any TEA/TEOA selectivity difference is fully explained by quenching kinetics, cobalt-state changes, or uncontrolled background reactions.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: P01 is adequate because it keeps the Co-bpy context while allowing donor substitution under one baseline; the key comparison is TEA versus TEOA with matched CO2 atmosphere and medium. Supplementary transfer to P02 is lower value here because homogeneous donor-side quenching there does not directly test substrate-associated adduct chemistry.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Direct observation of such intermediates in a TEA/TEOA Co-bpy comparison is absent from the supplied data, so this is a falsifiable transfer hypothesis rather than an established mechanism. Some related claims are author interpretations and may not generalize across metals or solvents.

candidate_menu.title: Matched TEA/TEOA benchmark
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether TEA-versus-TEOA substitution alone reproducibly changes CO/H2 distribution in the P01 CoCl2+bpy/g-C3N4 MeCN/H2O platform. This first establishes whether the reported difference survives strict matching before mechanism-focused interpretation.
candidate_menu.method: Run side-by-side P01 photocatalysis with the literature-grounded TEOA baseline and a TEA-only comparator while holding catalyst, ligand, g-C3N4, solvent ratio, CO2 handling, illumination, reactor geometry, and GC workflow fixed; quantify CO and H2 together and preferably as time courses rather than one endpoint only.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Directly addresses the core claim versus the alternative that apparent donor effects collapse under tighter comparability controls. It yields the primary comparative readout but cannot by itself distinguish donor photophysics from proton-management or cobalt-state causes.

candidate_menu.title: Necessity controls and backgrounds
candidate_menu.purpose: Determine whether observed CO/H2 in the matched benchmark requires the intended photocatalytic system and whether background formation differs enough to distort the TEA/TEOA comparison. This separates additive-specific comparison from simple artifact or support-only photochemistry.
candidate_menu.method: Within the same matched assay framework, include dark, Ar/no-CO2, no-cobalt, no-bpy, no-g-C3N4, and no-amine conditions for both donor settings where applicable; analyze CO and H2 by the same gas method and compare background fractions to the full system.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Omission tests necessity, not donor specificity, and bounds whether catalyst-free or donor/photosensitizer background H2 or CO could compress the apparent TEA/TEOA selectivity gap. It also identifies which components must remain fixed in later mechanistic experiments.

candidate_menu.title: Donor amount series
candidate_menu.purpose: Ask whether any TEA/TEOA difference is intrinsic to donor identity or mainly reflects different effective donor/base or medium regimes. If the difference shrinks across matched amount series, condition-dependence becomes more plausible than a fixed identity effect.
candidate_menu.method: For TEA and TEOA separately, vary only donor loading around the P01 baseline while keeping all other formulation and operating variables fixed; compare CO amount, H2 amount, and CO/H2 selectivity surfaces rather than single-point values.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This is an amount-variation intervention, not an omission or identity substitution, and it tests whether donor identity effects persist after exploring comparable donor windows. It is especially relevant because medium composition and amine proportion are reported to alter CO/H2 outputs in related cobalt systems.

candidate_menu.title: Donor-side quenching comparison
candidate_menu.purpose: Assess whether TEA and TEOA differ in upstream photoredox behavior under matched catalyst-containing conditions, providing a discriminating covariate for any catalytic product shift. Similar quenching despite different CO/H2 would weaken a purely donor-photophysics explanation.
candidate_menu.method: Apply transferable fluorescence and/or UV-vis quenching measurements to the matched baseline and TEA-substituted formulations, using the same absorber-containing sample state with and without cobalt components as references; if feasible, include a cleaner supplementary P02 homogeneous assay to validate directionality of donor effects.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This characterization does not prove mechanism but tests whether donor substitution measurably changes the electron-transfer entry step that could feed the cobalt manifold. It helps discriminate upstream donor effects from downstream proton or catalyst-state explanations.

candidate_menu.title: Cobalt state under each donor
candidate_menu.purpose: Check whether TEA and TEOA produce different cobalt-state or coordination signatures during or near operation, which would support a donor-linked change in the catalytic manifold rather than only a bulk assay artifact. Null differences would not exclude all mechanisms but would narrow them.
candidate_menu.method: Use near-operando or operando-accessible spectroscopy on matched P01 samples before illumination and under irradiation, with catalyst-free or donor-free references where needed for assignment; prioritize methods transferable for cobalt/environment changes rather than recovered-sample-only inference.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Provides descriptive state information complementary to product data and can reveal donor-correlated cobalt changes without claiming causal proof of the active species. Its interpretability is limited by unresolved exact active-state identity in P01.

candidate_menu.title: CO origin check by donor
candidate_menu.purpose: Verify that CO observed under each donor condition is CO2-derived and not a donor-specific carbon artifact, especially if TEA and TEOA give different CO outputs. This protects the central comparison from overinterpreting donor-dependent side chemistry as altered CO2 reduction selectivity.
candidate_menu.method: Repeat the matched benchmark with reproducible 13CO2 labeling and GC-MS or equivalent isotopic product analysis for the TEA and TEOA cases, alongside the established negative controls from the benchmark set.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This experiment bounds origin claims rather than explaining why TEA and TEOA differ; a positive CO2-origin result still leaves donor-side, proton-management, and cobalt-state explanations open. It is most valuable if significant CO is observed in both donor conditions or if donor-specific CO backgrounds are suspected.

candidate_menu.title: Matched donor quenching in P01
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether TEA-for-TEOA substitution changes absorber-side quenching or bleaching behavior in the primary Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system under otherwise fixed composition. A donor-dependent photophysical shift aligning with catalytic selectivity would support, but not prove, upstream electron-delivery involvement.
candidate_menu.method: Measure steady-state fluorescence and/or UV-vis changes for absorber-containing P01 suspensions or filtrates with TEOA versus TEA, including no-cobalt and no-donor references to separate donor quenching from cobalt-associated pathways and background optical changes.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This is the most direct within-platform characterization of whether donor identity alters the entry photoredox step rather than only downstream chemistry. Similar quenching observables for TEA and TEOA would weaken a purely upstream explanation for any CO/H2 difference.

candidate_menu.title: Transient reduced-state comparison
candidate_menu.purpose: Ask whether TEA and TEOA generate different transient reduced-state amplitudes or lifetimes under illumination, which would indicate altered electron flux into catalytic intermediates. Divergent transient behavior with matched formulation would be stronger support for H02 than steady-state quenching alone.
candidate_menu.method: Apply time-resolved transient absorption or analogous charge-carrier spectroscopy to matched P01 donor conditions, using dark and no-donor backgrounds and treating assignments as provisional unless corroborated by catalyst-free or absorber-only references.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This adds kinetic/state information beyond bulk quenching by probing reduced intermediates or long-lived electrons under operating-relevant conditions. It can discriminate altered electron-delivery dynamics from unchanged upstream photophysics, but not by itself assign the exact active cobalt species.

candidate_menu.title: Supplementary P02 quenching transfer
candidate_menu.purpose: Use the more chemically defined homogeneous cobalt/Ru/TEOA platform as a supplementary check on whether TEA versus TEOA measurably changes donor-side quenching behavior when support effects are minimized. Agreement in direction with P01 would strengthen transfer of an upstream donor effect; disagreement would point to platform-specific or downstream causes.
candidate_menu.method: Within P02, substitute TEA for TEOA while holding cobalt catalyst, Ru photosensitizer, solvent family, CO2 saturation, and illumination fixed, then compare Stern-Volmer or equivalent quenching observables with matched blanks and without over-transferring absolute rates back to P01.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This is a substitution experiment in a supplementary system, not a replacement platform, and it tests whether donor identity affects a cleaner quenching manifold already supported by source evidence. Its value is comparative directionality, not proof that P01 shares the same detailed mechanism.

candidate_menu.title: Photophysics-to-products correlation
candidate_menu.purpose: Determine whether donor-dependent quenching or transient observables covary with donor-dependent CO/H2 outputs across the matched TEA and TEOA conditions. Correlation would support H02, whereas product differences without corresponding upstream changes would favor downstream explanations.
candidate_menu.method: Link the readouts from matched catalytic benchmarking and donor-side characterization by collecting both datasets on the same baseline and comparator formulations, comparing direction and reproducibility of changes rather than inferring causality from a single metric.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This experiment integrates descriptive photophysics with catalytic performance, which is the key discriminating prediction of H02. It still cannot exclude coupled proton-management or cobalt-state effects if multiple observables shift together.

candidate_menu.title: Donor radical detection by substitution
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA produce detectably different donor-derived radical signatures under irradiation, which would support different reductive-quenching routes or follow-up chemistry. Absence of a resolved difference would leave H02 open if radicals are short-lived or spectroscopically obscured.
candidate_menu.method: Use transferable EPR spin-trapping or related radical-detection measurements on illuminated donor-containing formulations, comparing TEA and TEOA under matched solvent and light conditions with dark and no-absorber controls and acknowledging donor-viscosity effects on line shape.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This specifically probes donor-derived reactive intermediates rather than only net quenching efficiency, giving mechanistic texture to any donor-side difference. It is a substitution characterization, not a catalytic readout, and transfer to the Co-bpy system requires pilot validation.

candidate_menu.title: Medium-normalized TEA vs TEOA
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether a TEA/TEOA selectivity difference persists after tighter matching of solvent and proton-delivery conditions in P01 rather than only nominal donor substitution. If the CO/H2 contrast contracts under normalized composition, that supports a medium/proton-management contribution without proving the detailed cause.
candidate_menu.method: Run the matched P01 benchmark with TEA and TEOA while explicitly holding MeCN/H2O ratio, total amine-derived volume fraction, CO2 handling, cobalt/bpy/g-C3N4 loadings, and analysis fixed; compare CO, H2, and CO/H2 time profiles across the donor pair under the original and composition-normalized settings.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This is the key comparative intervention for H03 because it asks whether donor identity effects survive stronger control of variables linked in the literature to proton supply, dissolved CO2, viscosity, and local medium. It discriminates medium-coupled association from a donor effect that remains robust after normalization.

candidate_menu.title: Isotope-sensitive operando signatures
candidate_menu.purpose: Ask whether TEA and TEOA produce different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic features under CO2 reduction conditions, consistent with different hydrogen-containing or proton-coupled states. A donor-dependent isotope response would support, but not uniquely assign, a proton-management explanation.
candidate_menu.method: Acquire operando or near-operando IR and/or complementary spectroscopy on matched P01 TEA and TEOA samples under CO2 with H2O versus D2O substitution, using donor-free and dark references where feasible and treating peak assignments as provisional unless isotope shifts and controls agree.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This characterization targets the discriminating prediction that the donor effect should track isotope-sensitive observables if proton delivery or hydrogen-containing intermediates differ. It cannot by itself exclude cobalt-state or donor-redox differences if several processes shift together.

candidate_menu.title: CO2-associated donor speciation
candidate_menu.purpose: Determine whether TEA and TEOA generate different CO2-associated solution states before or during illumination, such as amine-CO2 or donor-linked adduct signatures, under otherwise matched P01 medium. Detectable donor-specific CO2-associated signals would support a local substrate-environment contribution.
candidate_menu.method: Measure donor-containing P01 media with and without CO2 saturation, before illumination and under reaction-relevant equilibration, using solution IR and/or NMR style readouts transferable for CO2-associated speciation; compare TEA, TEOA, and no-amine references while keeping solvent composition fixed.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This descriptive experiment addresses whether the donors differ in substrate-associated chemistry rather than only electron donation. Positive differences would still be associational unless later linked to catalytic output under the same matched conditions.

candidate_menu.title: Amine omission and inert-base replacement
candidate_menu.purpose: Separate amine necessity from amine specificity by testing whether product formation requires the donor/additive and whether a non-donor pH/base adjustment can mimic part of the TEA/TEOA effect. This distinguishes omission from substitution and bounds how much of the donor effect could reflect bulk basicity alone.
candidate_menu.method: In the P01 assay, compare full TEA and TEOA runs to no-amine controls and to conditions where an added non-sacrificial base or proton-balancing adjustment is introduced without replacing the donor role; quantify CO and H2 with the same workflow and interpret only bounded descriptive rescue or non-rescue outcomes.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: No-amine tests necessity, whereas inert-base replacement tests whether proton-management or base environment can partially substitute for donor identity; these answer different questions. Because a non-donor base cannot replicate reductive quenching, any partial rescue would support a mixed-function explanation rather than full equivalence.

candidate_menu.title: Water-fraction crossover map
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether the TEA/TEOA selectivity contrast depends strongly on water content, as expected if proton availability and local medium govern the observed donor effect. A crossover or collapse across water fraction would favor H03 over a donor-identity effect that is largely water-insensitive.
candidate_menu.method: For each donor in P01, vary only the MeCN/H2O composition around the baseline while holding catalyst, ligand, g-C3N4, nominal donor condition, CO2 handling, and illumination fixed; collect CO and H2 outputs together and, where possible, paired medium descriptors such as pH/pD or conductivity.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This is a comparative medium intervention rather than a donor-amount series, designed to reveal whether donor identity interacts with proton-source richness or solvent environment. It is especially informative if TEA and TEOA differ at one water fraction but converge at another.

candidate_menu.title: Proton-readout correlation set
candidate_menu.purpose: Link donor-dependent catalytic selectivity to directly measured medium/proton-related covariates rather than inferring them from composition alone. Correlation of CO/H2 shifts with donor-dependent pH/pD, conductivity, or related bulk descriptors would support H03 but remain non-causal without the matched interventions.
candidate_menu.method: On the same TEA and TEOA formulations used for catalytic comparisons, record pre- and post-irradiation bulk medium descriptors accessible in P01, such as pH or pD proxies, conductivity, and gas uptake-relevant equilibration measures, then compare their direction of change with CO and H2 outputs.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This adds bounded descriptive measurements that can explain whether TEA and TEOA actually create different proton-management environments under matched nominal recipes. It cannot identify the microscopic intermediate, but it helps interpret whether later isotope or substitution results are plausibly medium-driven.

candidate_menu.title: Operando cobalt-state comparison
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA give different cobalt oxidation-state or coordination signatures under matched P01 turnover conditions. A reproducible donor-dependent difference would support cobalt-manifold involvement, whereas indistinguishable signatures would weaken but not fully exclude H04.
candidate_menu.method: Apply operando or near-operando Co-focused XAS and/or complementary UV-vis on the same baseline and TEA-substituted P01 formulations before illumination and during reaction, using no-cobalt, no-donor, and dark references to bound assignment and avoid relying only on recovered samples.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Provides the closest direct test of the H04 prediction by asking whether donor substitution changes observable cobalt state during operation rather than only products. It remains descriptive if multiple cobalt species coexist or signals are too weak for unique assignment.

candidate_menu.title: Donor binding and preassembly test
candidate_menu.purpose: Ask whether TEA and TEOA differ in their direct interaction with the cobalt-bpy formulation before irradiation, which could predispose different catalytic states. This distinguishes possible donor coordination/preassociation from later photochemical divergence.
candidate_menu.method: Measure matched P01 precursor mixtures and simplified cobalt-bpy solution analogues with incremental TEA or TEOA addition using spectrophotometric titration and, where feasible, 1H NMR-style comparison to look for donor-dependent shifts or association signatures against donor-free references.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This addresses pre-turnover specificity of donor identity rather than necessity, and it can reveal whether the two amines are chemically nonequivalent toward cobalt even before catalysis begins. Positive association would not prove that the bound form is active under irradiation.

candidate_menu.title: Deactivation and catalyst persistence map
candidate_menu.purpose: Determine whether TEA and TEOA produce different cobalt deactivation or persistence trends that parallel CO/H2 behavior. Divergent time-dependent loss of activity or cobalt-state drift would support H04 over a purely upstream donor-photophysics explanation.
candidate_menu.method: Run matched time-course photocatalysis in P01 with intermittent product analysis and paired pre/during/post reaction cobalt-state measurements on the same donor conditions, comparing donor-dependent decay profiles rather than only endpoint selectivity.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Integrates stability and product readouts to ask whether donor identity changes catalyst survival or conversion to another active/inactive form. It can discriminate donor-linked deactivation trends, but not by itself identify the exact decomposition product.

candidate_menu.title: Operando IR/EPR donor-adduct screen
candidate_menu.purpose: Probe whether TEA and TEOA generate different donor-associated cobalt or substrate-bound intermediates under reaction conditions, including possibilities that TEOA forms adduct-like species absent with TEA. Donor-specific signatures would support a speciation-based contribution to the product shift.
candidate_menu.method: Use in situ IR and/or EPR on matched P01 donor conditions under CO2 and illumination, with donor-free, dark, and no-cobalt controls and cautious assignment criteria because transferred precedent comes from non-cobalt or nonidentical systems.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Adds orthogonal observables for donor-linked intermediate or adduct chemistry that XAS alone may miss. It is especially useful if TEA and TEOA differ without a large bulk cobalt oxidation-state contrast.

candidate_menu.title: P02 state-readout bridge
candidate_menu.purpose: Use the supplementary homogeneous cobalt platform to test whether TEA-for-TEOA substitution changes cobalt-state or donor-coupled spectroscopic behavior in a cleaner medium where support effects are reduced. Agreement in donor-dependent state trends with P01 would strengthen transfer; disagreement would suggest platform-specific speciation.
candidate_menu.method: Within P02, substitute TEA for TEOA while holding cobalt catalyst, Ru photosensitizer, solvent family, CO2 saturation, and illumination fixed, then collect quenching plus cobalt-state-sensitive spectra with matched blanks and compare only qualitative directionality to P01.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This does not replace the primary system; it asks whether donor-linked cobalt-state differences are intrinsic enough to survive in a more chemically defined assay. Its inferential value is bounded because catalyst architecture differs from the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target.

candidate_menu.title: Ligand and support omission around donor effect
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether any donor-dependent cobalt-state signature requires the full Co-bpy/support assembly or appears already in partial formulations. This separates dependence on bpy or g-C3N4 from donor identity itself and helps localize where speciation divergence emerges.
candidate_menu.method: Compare TEA and TEOA in matched cobalt-containing formulations that omit bpy or omit g-C3N4 one factor at a time, measuring cobalt-state observables and bounded product/background outputs under the same analytical workflow rather than interpreting joint omissions mechanistically.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: These are omission experiments, not donor substitutions, and they answer whether donor-linked state differences are contingent on ligand or support context. They can block overassignment of a donor effect to cobalt speciation when the observed change actually depends on another component.

candidate_menu.title: CO2-adduct speciation by donor
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether TEOA and TEA give different CO2-associated solution or catalyst-linked signatures under the matched P01 medium before illumination, which is the core transferable prediction of H05. A donor-specific signal would support substrate-associated chemistry but remain associational until linked to catalysis.
candidate_menu.method: Compare TEA-, TEOA-, and no-amine P01 media with and without CO2 using transferable IR and/or NMR-style speciation readouts under fixed solvent composition and matched cobalt/bpy presence, using assignment controls that distinguish bulk amine-CO2 species from possible catalyst-associated adducts where resolution permits.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This is the most direct descriptive test of the proposed non-innocent donor role because it asks whether the donor changes observable CO2-associated states even before invoking different quenching. It cannot by itself prove that any detected adduct is on-pathway for CO formation.

candidate_menu.title: Operando isotope-sensitive IR
candidate_menu.purpose: Ask whether TEA and TEOA differ in intermediate-associated operando vibrational features under CO2 reduction conditions, and whether isotope substitution supports assignment of hydrogen-containing or CO2-derived species. This targets the prediction that donor identity changes substrate/intermediate stabilization rather than only electron delivery.
candidate_menu.method: Acquire near-operando or operando IR on matched P01 TEA and TEOA runs under CO2, adding 13CO2 and/or H2O-to-D2O substitution where feasible with dark, no-cobalt, and no-donor references to bound assignments and avoid overcalling overlapping bands.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: Compared with bulk pre-equilibrium speciation, this probes reaction-state signatures and uses isotopic shifts to discriminate assignments. It remains descriptive if multiple overlapping intermediates respond together or signal intensity is insufficient.

candidate_menu.title: Origin-bounded donor comparison
candidate_menu.purpose: Determine whether any TEA/TEOA difference in CO output persists when CO origin is explicitly bounded as CO2-derived, reducing the risk that donor-specific side chemistry is misread as altered CO2-reduction selectivity. This is especially relevant because TEOA-related side chemistry is reported in other systems.
candidate_menu.method: Repeat the matched TEA versus TEOA P01 benchmark under 13CO2 with isotopic CO analysis while recording CO and H2 together and retaining the usual no-CO2 and dark controls, then compare donor-dependent selectivity only within the CO2-origin-confirmed fraction.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This does not test adduct identity directly, but it bounds a key alternative that donor decomposition or background carbon could explain apparent donor effects. A confirmed CO2 origin still leaves adduct stabilization, cobalt-state, and quenching explanations open.

candidate_menu.title: Adduct signal versus quenching
candidate_menu.purpose: Discriminate H05 from a purely upstream quenching explanation by asking whether donor-dependent substrate-associated signatures appear even when donor-side electron-supply observables are similar. This is the central causal contrast stated in the hypothesis.
candidate_menu.method: On the same matched TEA and TEOA formulations, pair the substrate/intermediate readouts from E25 or E26 with donor-side quenching observables already established for the platform, comparing whether a donor-specific adduct/intermediate contrast survives despite similar quenching behavior.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This experiment is comparative integration rather than a new standalone assay, and its value is in separating downstream substrate-associated differences from upstream photophysical similarity. If both adduct-like and quenching observables shift together, discrimination remains limited.

candidate_menu.title: Amine omission and inert-donor contrast
candidate_menu.purpose: Separate necessity of the multifunctional amine from specificity of TEOA versus TEA for substrate-associated chemistry. Omission asks whether the amine-linked signatures require donor presence at all, while substitution asks whether TEOA produces a qualitatively different CO2-associated state than TEA.
candidate_menu.method: Measure the same speciation or operando signatures in full TEOA, full TEA, and no-amine P01 formulations under matched CO2 exposure, and where feasible include a bounded non-TEOA amine condition only as a descriptive contrast without claiming functional equivalence in electron donation.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This explicitly distinguishes omission from substitution, which answer different questions for H05. It can show whether TEOA-specific signatures are genuinely donor-identity dependent rather than generic consequences of having any amine present.

candidate_menu.title: Cobalt-linked adduct screen
candidate_menu.purpose: Test whether any donor-specific substrate-associated signal is accompanied by donor-specific cobalt-state or coordination changes, helping distinguish amine-only CO2 capture from catalyst-linked adduct or intermediate stabilization. This narrows where the hypothesized non-innocent chemistry resides.
candidate_menu.method: Use matched P01 TEA and TEOA samples under CO2 for paired cobalt-sensitive spectroscopy and intermediate-sensitive IR/EPR-style monitoring, with no-cobalt and dark references to determine whether the donor-dependent signal requires cobalt and whether cobalt observables shift in parallel.
candidate_menu.distinct_information: This cross-check is important because H05 allows either amine-linked or catalyst-linked substrate chemistry, and the inference differs between them. Null cobalt dependence would weaken a catalyst-adduct interpretation without excluding bulk donor-CO2 interactions.

candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA benchmark
candidates.purpose: Test whether changing the amine from TEOA to TEA alone alters CO/H2 distribution in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform under intentionally unmatched conditions to maximize donor contrast.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 and GX012 motivate a cobalt-containing photocatalytic CO2-reduction comparison using TEOA and TEA. EV063 suggests medium can matter, so the proposal transfers this by changing donor identity while also allowing donor-driven medium differences to remain, treating any resulting product shift as additive-specific. EV081, EV045, and EV022 support measuring CO and H2 together and including simple catalytic context controls.

If the difference appears only when cobalt components are present, that further supports involvement of cobalt-associated interactions but still does not establish the catalytic mechanism.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference within calibrated detection limits in both cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matched matrices, a large donor-specific upstream optical difference is disfavored as the main explanation for any CO/H2 shift, while leaving downstream proton management, catalyst speciation, and assay artifacts unresolved.

A measured optical difference is also inconclusive for catalytic causation unless linked separately to catalytic data.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the verified P01 baseline identities and nominal component levels as the starting point. Any dilution or path-length adjustment needed for optical work must be applied equally across all groups and documented as an adaptation from the catalytic matrix. candidates.limitations: This is characterization, not a catalytic readout. In a g-C3N4-containing or otherwise scattering matrix, fluorescence and UV-vis assignments can be compromised by adsorption, inner-filter effects, and turbidity. Even with cobalt-free controls, the experiment cannot identify the turnover-relevant intermediate or prove that a donor-dependent optical change causes a donor-dependent CO/H2 shift. Transfer from EV053, EV065, GX007, and EV011 is methodological and donor-chemistry based, not direct proof for the exact P01 catalytic manifold.

candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 directly anchors the CoCl2+bpy/g-C3N4/MeCN:H2O/TEOA platform and notes TEA as a related donor option. The proposal therefore compares TEA and TEOA within one anchored formulation family, adds no-amine and Ar controls for attribution, and narrows inference because composition normalization cannot make TEA and TEOA chemically equivalent.

comparisons.inference: Descriptive anchored comparison: whether an apparent TEA/TEOA selectivity difference is reproduced in the literature-linked recipe.
Primary bounded comparison: if a difference remains after the defined composition normalization, donor identity or other donor-linked properties still matter within this constrained recipe family.
Normalization-effect check within TEOA; this multi-factor contrast shows whether normalization itself changes output and therefore how strongly the anchored comparison was composition-sensitive.
Normalization-effect check within TEA; large changes indicate that the unnormalized donor comparison was materially confounded by recipe composition.
CO2-attribution control for the normalized TEOA condition; CO observed mainly under CO2 supports assignment of carbon-containing products to the intended feed rather than background contamination.
CO2-attribution control for the normalized TEA condition; H2 may persist under Ar, so this contrast mainly bounds carbon-product attribution rather than hydrogen pathways.
Necessity-oriented comparison for added amine in the normalized TEOA recipe family, but not a single-factor causal test because amine removal also changes total liquid composition logic.
Necessity-oriented comparison for added amine in the normalized TEA recipe family, likewise confounded by composition change and therefore bounded to functional necessity rather than mechanism.

procedure: Select one executable P01 baseline from EV059, then pilot catalyst loading, g-C3N4 amount, reactor fill, and sampling times to obtain quantifiable CO and H2 without detector saturation or immediate deactivation.

Prepare all groups with the same cobalt source, bpy source, g-C3N4 batch, reactor geometry, illumination program, and analytical workflow; for E13G03-E13G06 explicitly match MeCN/H2O and total amine-derived fraction across TEA and TEOA normalized groups.
Run the irradiations under identical timing and temperature control, sampling headspace at common time points for CO and H2 in one calibration campaign that includes the Ar and no-amine groups.
Report CO amount, H2 amount, and CO/H2 time profiles for every group, and record bulk pre- and post-run apparent pH plus visible phase or precipitation changes only as comparability covariates.

Interpret the normalized TEA versus TEOA contrast narrowly, using the control groups to confirm baseline attribution and to avoid reading any selectivity collapse as proof of one specific hidden variable.
measurements: Gas-phase CO amount versus time.
Gas-phase H2 amount versus time.
CO/H2 ratio or selectivity versus time calculated from jointly measured products.
Bulk pre- and post-run apparent pH of the liquid phase as a covariate only.
Qualitative notes on color change, precipitation, or phase separation as comparability checks only.
Analytical blank and calibration stability across the full sample set.
candidates.supports: Supports the medium-dominant version of H03 only in a narrowed sense if a TEA/TEOA difference evident in the anchored recipe becomes substantially smaller or disappears in the normalized comparison, while the CO2 and no-amine controls show that the normalized experiment still produces attributable signal. This would indicate that recipe-linked medium effects contribute materially, without identifying which hidden variable is responsible.
candidates.refutes: Refutes the stronger medium-dominant emphasis of H03 if the TEA/TEOA difference is reproduced with similar direction and magnitude in both anchored and normalized comparisons, suggesting that the controlled composition variables are not the main source of the selectivity difference. That outcome would be more compatible with donor-specific redox, coordination, or cobalt-state alternatives, though not uniquely proving any one of them.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if one or more normalized groups give signal near detection limits, if normalization causes incompatible catalyst stability or phase behavior, if the Ar or no-amine controls reveal strong background artifacts, or if the observed TEA/TEOA differences are comparable to run-to-run analytical uncertainty.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature values. Use the EV059-linked recipe family only to choose the starting composition logic, then pilot the minimum necessary executable settings: catalyst loading window, support amount, irradiation time, sampling interval, and gas calibration range. For normalized groups, hold MeCN/H2O ratio and total amine-derived fraction constant across TEA and TEOA where physically feasible; if miscibility or handling prevents exact matching, document the deviation and narrow the inference rather than asserting equivalence.
candidates.limitations: TEA and TEOA remain chemically nonequivalent even after composition normalization, so this card cannot isolate proton activity, dissolved CO2, viscosity, conductivity, and cobalt coordination effects from one another. The no-amine comparison also changes overall liquid composition and therefore tests functional necessity more than pure mechanistic causality. Product data alone cannot identify the active cobalt species or the dominant hidden variable behind any selectivity shift.

candidates.title: Isotope-sensitive operando signatures in TEA vs TEOA Co-bpy photocatalysis
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA produce different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic observables under one matched P01 configuration, consistent with different proton-coupled environments or hydrogen-containing states, while avoiding overclaim that isotope effects identify a unique intermediate.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV080 supports isotope substitution as a transferable assignment aid in operando FTIR-type measurements, not species identity in this Co-bpy system. GX010 and GX015 support proton-inventory and isotope logic as transferable discriminators of proton-delivery environments in cobalt CO2-reduction chemistry, but not direct proof for this photocatalyst. EV031 supports the transferable idea that donor or solvent environment can change detectable intermediate populations and selectivity in bipyridine-based CO2 reduction. Proposed transfer: use one preselected operando or near-operando spectroscopic mode for matched TEA and TEOA samples, compare H2O-containing and D2O-containing media within each donor, and interpret any isotope-sensitive donor difference only as evidence for differing hydrogen-coupled observables under these conditions.

Prepare matched TEA and TEOA P01 samples from the same cobalt source, bpy source, g-C3N4 batch, solvent family, gas handling, and optical geometry; include donor-free background if signal quality remains acceptable.

Pilot path length, catalyst loading, aqueous fraction, and acquisition timing using prespecified criteria of unsaturated spectra, repeatable baseline, and acceptable suspension scattering; reject settings that differentially degrade TEA versus TEOA baseline quality.

Isotope-induced shifts, attenuation, or altered temporal evolution after H2O-to-D2O substitution within each donor condition
Difference spectra against dark, pre-illumination, and donor-free references to identify background or support-derived contributions
Replicate agreement of donor-dependent isotope responses across independently prepared samples
Parallel CO and H2 product amounts from matched runs to test co-occurrence with selectivity differences without equating correlation to cause
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent isotope response under matched acquisition: TEA and TEOA differ in H/D-sensitive band positions, magnitudes, or time behavior beyond donor-free or baseline changes. Stronger but still non-decisive support occurs if donor-dependent CO and H2 divergence also changes in pattern under the same isotopic substitution.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, while spectra are dominated by shared or non-isotope-sensitive changes. If catalytic TEA and TEOA differences remain substantial in matched runs despite indistinguishable H/D-sensitive signatures, a proton-management-centered explanation is weakened relative to alternatives.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if suspension scattering or baseline drift obscures donor comparisons, if overlapping support or solvent features dominate assignment, if D2O substitution changes bulk medium properties enough that spectral differences cannot be bounded to hydrogen-coupled observables, or if donor-dependent changes are present but not isotope-sensitive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-anchored P01 formulation family only after verifying the exact baseline composition from supplied source records. Calibrate path length, catalyst loading, aqueous fraction, and acquisition interval by pilot criteria of stable baseline, detectable catalyst-region signal, and repeatable spectra across replicate preparations. Predefine acceptable baseline-drift and scattering thresholds before comparing donors. Keep preparation order and nominal component identities matched between H2O-containing and D2O-containing groups. If pH or pD matching is attempted, document one convention and use it consistently without claiming exact equivalence.
candidates.limitations: This card can test whether TEA and TEOA differ in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, but it cannot uniquely identify intermediates, prove rate-determining roles, or isolate proton management from all donor-dependent medium changes. D2O substitution is itself a multi-property perturbation, and near-operando measurements may miss the true operating state.

GX009 adds transferable concern that cobalt-bipyridine media can change with solvent coordination, water, viscosity, and conductivity. candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference in CO2-responsive spectral features under matched P01 medium, especially if TEOA and TEA show distinct changes relative to their own inert references and the no-amine background. This would support a local CO2/proton-environment contribution, while remaining associational until linked to catalytic outcomes under the same controls.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03-dominant interpretation would be no reproducible donor-specific CO2-responsive difference despite adequate detection sensitivity and clean backgrounds, especially if TEA and TEOA appear spectroscopically similar under matched medium. That would weaken the case that donor-linked CO2-associated speciation is a main explanation, though it would not prove a redox-only mechanism.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if spectra are dominated by solvent/support overlap, if signals are near detection limits, if assignments depend on a single ambiguous band, or if donor substitution also changes uncontrolled covariates enough that the contrast becomes multi-factor in practice. Observing a new signal without assignment controls cannot establish adduct identity or catalytic relevance.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent fixed acquisition settings. Pilot first to choose sample concentration, path length, equilibration time, and whether IR, NMR, or both have usable signal-to-background in the actual P01 medium. Set the lowest concentration that still gives reproducible donor and CO2-responsive features without obvious precipitation or severe scattering from g-C3N4. Use the same preparation order, gas-contact protocol, and delay before measurement across groups. If g-C3N4 prevents interpretable solution-state spectra, run a matched clarified-supernatant variant as a bounded adaptation and label the transfer limitation explicitly rather than claiming fully equivalent operating chemistry.
candidates.limitations: This characterization is descriptive. A donor-specific CO2-responsive signal cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate, the active cobalt state, or the cause of CO/H2 selectivity. g-C3N4 and cobalt-bpy may contribute overlapping features, and dark-equilibrated samples may miss illumination-generated states. If donor identity changes pH, coordination, or suspension properties simultaneously, the comparison remains mechanistically mixed even when composition is nominally matched.

candidates.purpose: Test whether amine presence is necessary in the P01 TEA/TEOA comparison and whether a tightly screened non-donor base can produce only limited medium-related shifts, without treating it as an amine surrogate or proof of proton-management causality.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV013 supports treating TEA and TEOA as multifunctional additives that can act as H+ source and hole scavenger, so omission is required before interpreting additive identity effects. EV024, GX010, and GX015 support the narrower transferable idea that proton-delivery environment can alter CO2-reduction behavior, which justifies a bounded non-donor-base probe. GX008 supports matched negative controls and broad product analysis. Transfer remains limited because no supplied evidence shows that a non-donor base reproduces the sacrificial-donor role in the target Co-bpy photocatalysis; therefore any shift with base addition is only descriptive evidence for medium contribution.

candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 would be that TEA and TEOA show a similar directional CO/H2 difference of comparable magnitude at both water settings while each donor is otherwise stable and analytically well matched. That would favor an explanation dominated by donor-specific redox or cobalt-state effects that are not substantially collapsed by this medium normalization.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include very low product formation, unstable phase behavior, unequal catalyst suspension or light absorption across water settings, analytical uncertainty larger than the donor effect, or simultaneous large changes in conductivity/dispersion that prevent attributing differences specifically to proton-management versus other medium changes.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent solvent fractions. Choose two water settings by pilot within the literature-supported MeCN/H2O family: one near the current baseline and one more water-rich, but only if both remain operationally comparable for TEA and TEOA. Hold total solvent volume constant. Keep the same nominal donor condition for TEA and TEOA as an initial comparator, then verify by pilot that neither donor causes immediate deactivation, phase separation, or complete quenching failure. If apparent pH is not reliable in the mixed solvent, record it only as a bounded descriptor and prioritize conductivity and product outputs.

Even single-factor pairwise contrasts are embedded in a system where effective photon absorption and cobalt speciation may shift with medium. A crossover is therefore strong descriptive evidence for medium involvement but not proof of a specific proton-relay or CO2-adduct mechanism. In situ or rapid-freeze or rapid-transfer EPR spectra, tracking appearance, disappearance, g-pattern changes, and line broadening under TEA versus TEOA conditions.
Matched catalytic readouts from parallel or same-batch experiments: CO and H2 amounts or rates, reported together rather than selectivity alone.
Background spectra from donor-free, no-cobalt, and dark controls for both donors to establish which signals are not cobalt-specific or not light-dependent.

candidates.supports: H04 is supported if, under the locked matched P01 comparison, TEA and TEOA show reproducibly different cobalt-requiring and light-dependent IR and or EPR signatures, or different persistence or loss of such signatures over time, and those differences track a donor-dependent CO/H2 change better than donor-free, no-cobalt, or dark backgrounds do.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in cobalt-requiring, light-dependent IR/EPR observables within detection limits while catalytic CO/H2 still differs under the same matched conditions, favoring explanations upstream in donor photochemistry or downstream in proton or CO2 handling rather than cobalt-state divergence.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are too weak, dominated by background or support signals, changed by viscosity or other physical effects without cobalt specificity, or if donor-dependent signals appear but cannot be distinguished from donor decomposition, generic radical formation, or unsupported assignments. Correlation without clean symmetric controls also remains inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-backed P01 formulation family only for component identity, not exact invented numbers. First verify the baseline recipe from source records. Then run pilots to set sample concentration, path length, irradiation interval, and EPR acquisition mode by the rule that cobalt-containing samples must show stable unsaturated baselines and donor-free and no-cobalt controls must remain interpretable. If TEA and TEOA differ strongly in viscosity or optical density, adjust only the measurement configuration, not the chemical formulation, and document that this preserves matched chemistry while changing detection settings. Choose time points by a calibration run that captures pre-illumination, early illumination, and a later turnover window without exhausting the sample.
candidates.limitations: Assignments are transferred from nonidentical systems and may not map to Co-bpy. IR/EPR can reveal donor-dependent species or state changes but cannot alone establish the full catalytic mechanism, the exact structure of the active cobalt species, or product origin. TEA/TEOA physical-property differences can alter line shape and transport, so apparent spectral differences are not automatically chemical. Near-operando aliquots may miss the true instantaneous working state. No-cobalt controls are background screens, not full single-factor catalytic comparisons because total composition changes.

Proposed transfer is limited: this is a cleaner bridge assay, not the target Co-bpy/g-C3N4 chemistry, so agreement would support donor-linked state trends while disagreement could reflect platform-specific speciation.

candidates.supports: Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent change between E23G01 and E23G02 in cobalt-associated spectral or operando XAS observables that is absent or much smaller in the corresponding cobalt-free blanks, with the qualitative donor trend aligning with a donor-linked change in CO/H2 output. candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if E23G01 and E23G02 show indistinguishable cobalt-dependent spectra and quenching-corrected state readouts across the operando window, while catalytic differences persist or are explained by donor-only blank behavior. candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if donor substitution changes optical baselines, viscosity, solubility, or inner-filter behavior enough to prevent matched interpretation; if cobalt signals are below detection or dominated by broad unresolved features; if TEA and TEOA require materially different concentration windows to keep the assay stable; or if P02 shows donor effects but P01 comparison data are unavailable for bridging.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-defined P02 component identities and solvent family, but verify exact concentrations and illumination settings from the supplied source before execution. If any setting is still uncertain, choose it by pilot rules: maintain measurable CO/H2 within a short assay window, keep absorbance/emission in the instrument linear range, keep cobalt and photosensitizer solutions visibly homogeneous, and use one common setting for both donors whenever possible. candidates.limitations: Catalyst architecture differs from the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so this is a transfer test rather than a direct explanation of P01. Donor substitution can change medium properties and quenching simultaneously, and homogeneous average-state methods may not reveal minority active species. Cobalt-free blanks help bound but do not eliminate confounding. Spectral changes alone cannot establish exact coordination structures or prove causality for product selectivity.

candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 supports the CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4+TEOA formulation family in MeCN/H2O and motivates this as the closest source-anchored platform for donor comparison. GX008 supports explicit negative controls and paired characterization plus product analysis. EV081 shows that partial or no-catalyst systems can still produce CO and H2, so omission results must be treated as necessity/background tests rather than proof of mechanism. GX016 supports the transferable idea that cobalt-centered identity can shift product selectivity under TEOA photocatalysis, motivating tests of whether donor-linked effects persist or collapse when ligand or support is removed. The proposal transfers these observations into a controlled omission matrix in the P01-style system; it does not assume literature-established active-species identity or that omitted formulations are mechanistic continuations of the full catalyst.

candidates.supports: H04 is supported if the full assembly shows a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state observables or stability trends and that donor-linked difference weakens, disappears, or changes character in at least one omission pair, indicating dependence on ligand or support context. candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable cobalt-state and stability observables in the full assembly within method resolution, and the ligand-omission and support-omission donor pairs likewise show no reproducible donor-linked divergence despite measurable products. candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations, catalyst loadings, or illumination settings. candidates.limitations: Omission of bpy or g-C3N4 may generate qualitatively different cobalt species rather than partial versions of the full catalyst, so these are dependence tests, not continuity proofs. EV059 does not provide a direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in one frozen recipe, so baseline comparability still requires verification. Recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state, and generic spectral changes cannot by themselves identify the active species or exact coordination geometry.

candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if signals are too weak, unresolved, or irreproducible; if TEA and TEOA differ but only alongside uncontrolled pH, water-content, or solubility changes; or if spectra show donor-dependent bulk amine-CO2 speciation but cannot separate that from catalyst-associated adducts. candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible donor-dependent reaction-state IR differences beyond baseline noise or generic medium changes, or that apparent differences disappear once symmetric isotope and cobalt-absent controls are applied. candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are dominated by overlap, weak signals, or baseline drift; if D2O or 13CO2 causes broad perturbation without interpretable assignment value; if only one donor condition yields usable isotope-control data; or if donor-dependent bands cannot be separated from cobalt-free backgrounds. candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature conditions. Band assignment may remain ambiguous because donor, solvent, bicarbonate or carbonate, products, and cobalt-ligand features can overlap. Isotope substitution can alter kinetics as well as frequencies. Near-operando spectra may miss the true operating state, and operando IR alone cannot prove the primary quenching route, exact adduct identity, or whether a detected species is on-path rather than spectator. comparisons.inference: Primary single-factor comparison for reproducibility of TEA versus TEOA effects on CO/H2 and on any pilot-qualified observables. If quenching observables are similar within a pre-set repeatability bound yet catalytic outputs differ, H05 remains viable but unproven; if both catalytic and quenching observables are similar, the reported donor difference weakens.
